newsitem.title: SPAIN: Atypical factors take shine off Repsol Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Atypical factors take shine off Repsol Q1 earnings.

text.p: Lacklustre first quarter earnings dulled by one-off factors at recently-privatised Repsol are not expected to be mirrored in the energy group's full year results, analysts said on Wednesday.

On Tuesday Repsol posted a 12.3 percent fall in first-quarter 1997 attributable profit to 31.04 billion pesetas ($215.7 million), below analysts' forecasts for an around three percent dip. The firm said results were affected by an unusually mild winter, static liquid petroleum gas prices and higher depreciation charges.

"The fall in net profit was worse than anticipated due to the greater impact on the gas division, particularly on Repsol Butano, while the other divisions performed well," said Juan Carlos Calvo, analyst at Merrill Lynch Espana.

Exploration and Production operating profit rose threefold to 12.13 billion pesetas, Refining and Marketing results rose 13.1 percent and the Chemicals division saw operating profit rise to 7.25 billion pesetas versus 5.56 billion.
But Gas results fell by more than half to 10.94 billion pesetas.
Josep Prats of Ahorro Corporacion Financiera (ACF), was not concerned that the first quarter would have a strong effect on full year results.
"The fall in profit is due to one-offs such as the climate and the butane tariffs, whose effects for the rest of the year will be much more limited," he said.
"Forty percent of the impact of gas results is produced in the first quarter, so for the rest of the year will not be so negative" Prats said.
Both Merrill Lynch and Ahorro Corporaction expect Repsol to post a 10 percent increase in full 1997 results, up from 119.22 billion pesetas in 1996.
Poor quarterly figures did not dampen the shares' performance. At 1315 GMT, Repsol was 60 pesetas higher, 0.99 percent, to 6,100 while the Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 0.18 percent to 6,336.47.
"People have been expecting very bad results, and perhaps they had exaggerated. I think we could see the shares at 6,300 pesetas in the short term," a dealer at a Spanish bank said.
Shares had been subject to profit-taking following huge gains on a highly successful public share offering in April, dealers said.

"The stock had seen classic profit-taking after the end of the offering and after doubts about results when the company itself had warned they would be weak, so now it's simply catching up" ACF's Prats said.
In a mandatory statement to bourse authorities on April 25, the firm warned that three months to March results would be negatively affected by an unusually temperate winter.
